title: iSmash Everett email refresh — 2026-10-05
source: Microsoft Outlook Email connector search_messages and list_attachments
scope: Carney, Onesta LLC, NW Prime/Alex, iSmash corporate, Everett City, Quaint Oak, related plan/permit/fountain/loading-dock and Bay Alarm correspondence.
limitations: Bounded search refresh, not a complete forensic mailbox export. Only relevant returned messages included.

Email bodies are preserved in the representation supplied by the connector (including quoted chains), not original MIME/EML. The connector contentType label may say html although returned text is converted Markdown.
receivedDateTime is preserved in UTC. Narrative times are converted to America/Los_Angeles; quoted-header timezone is not assumed.
Attachment names, IDs and sizes are indexed. No PDF/image attachment payloads were downloaded to the local evidence folder in this refresh, and attachment contents were not reviewed.
No City filing, approval, work-start or completion claim is inferred from an attached drawing, proposed date or email silence.
Contains private correspondence and portal links; retain locally and redact sensitive links before external sharing.

body.content:
Hi Bharath,  
  
As mentioned previously, our new permit timeline is longer than yours.  
  
Our architect, Adam, noted that it could take a month or more to get city
approval due to a backlog:  
  
"It could be a month or more before we hear from the city. I do not have a
means to move them any quicker. \- Adam"  
  
Could you please check with your city inspector to see if there is any way to
combine the new permit with yours? Since all of this work is tied together for
the city inspection, combining them may allow us to proceed without treating
it as a separate project.  
  
Please note that we are providing this assistance as a courtesy to help you
open your store. While we cannot guarantee a specific timeline due to city
processing times, we are doing what we can to help move things along.  
  
Best regards,  
  
Alex Jo
